description: Compaction: message sizes, fold planning, the summary transcript and extension, survival of a summary, and what a fold writes from a provider reply. Pure functions in src/agent/compaction.ts, plus runCompaction driven with a stubbed provider. Each case names op; the fold cases stub fetch with the given status and body.

cases.name: exported constants
a plain message counts its text
an attachment counts its name and its content
a message with no content counts zero
characters count UTF-16 units as JavaScript does
conversation chars add up everything when nothing is folded
conversation chars count the summary instead of the folded messages
a stale summary past the end adds only the summary
plan: nothing to do while the conversation fits
plan: folds once over budget, from the start
plan: never folds the most recent messages
plan: folds up to a user message
plan: declines a fold too small to be worth the cache
plan: resumes from where the last fold stopped
plan: stops when the remainder is already small enough
plan: a budget of zero folds nothing
plan: a negative budget folds nothing
plan: a conversation shorter than the tail
plan: an empty conversation
plan: ignores a stale summary past the end
plan: honours a caller that wants a longer tail
plan: a minimum fold above the available span refuses
plan: a minimum fold of two accepts the same span
plan: a keep-recent larger than the conversation refuses
plan: keep-recent of zero may fold to the last user message
manual plan: folds everything but the last exchange
manual plan: nothing to fold in a single exchange
manual plan: continues after an earlier fold
folded tokens count the characters the fold covers
transcript labels who said what
transcript names attachments without including them
transcript caps a very long message
transcript says so for an empty message
transcript trims surrounding whitespace of a message
summary request asks for notes when there are none

expected.content:
You compress a conversation so it can be carried forward in a smaller space. You are not talking to anyone: you are writing notes that another assistant will rely on as its only record of what came before.

Write facts, not narration. "The user is working on a project and asked several questions" is worthless. "Budget is 4200 GBP; deadline 14 March; user rejected Postgres and chose SQLite" is what this is for.

Keep, in this order of priority: decisions reached and the reasons for them; names, numbers, dates, versions, paths, identifiers and exact quotes that matter; what the user is trying to achieve; anything the user asked for that has not been delivered yet; corrections the user made.

Drop: pleasantries, restatements, your own reasoning, anything already superseded by a later message.

Write plain prose or short dashed lines. No headings, no preamble, no closing remark. Do not address the user. Do not say "the conversation" or "in summary". Start with the first fact.

Write the notes for this conversation.

User: hello
